description: We are Team Minion Yuri, and our mission is simple: steal the moon. Until the shrink ray is ready, we're starting with the next best thing, the entire sky. We're building a web tool that lets anyone explore SPHEREx images and spot what moves and changes over time. Muhahaha.
summary:
SPHEREx Blink is a public web tool that turns NASA SPHEREx images into a blinking animation, so objects that move or change brightness stand out. You type a sky position or pick an object; we find every SPHEREx exposure of that spot in NASA's IRSA archive, align them, stack them per visit and play them as a loop on one brightness scale.

SPHEREx pixels are 6.2 arcseconds, so even the fastest star moves under two pixels a year. A zoom loupe, a difference view and a predicted proper-motion track make that visible. Because SPHEREx sees 102 infrared colours, you can also step through six detector arrays, view false colour and plot a spectrum: the cold brown dwarf WISE 0855 is invisible at short wavelengths and appears near 4.5 microns.

Twenty objects play instantly, with a sky map, a "Spot the mover" game, GIF export and shareable links. It needs no login, so anyone can explore the changing infrared sky.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

SPHEREx Blink lets anyone watch a patch of sky change over time in NASA SPHEREx data. Enter coordinates (decimal or sexagesimal) or a name, choose a field of view from 2 to 40 arcminutes, and the tool plays every SPHEREx visit of that spot as a loop.

HOW IT WORKS

A Python pipeline does the astronomy: (1) search NASA/IPAC IRSA for every SPHEREx exposure covering the position, (2) download only the small cutout needed instead of the full 65 MB file, (3) align every exposure onto one north-up grid, (4) stack the exposures of each visit into one clean frame, removing cosmic rays and flagged pixels, (5) put all frames of a detector array on one brightness scale, so a steady star varies only 3-4% and only real change blinks. The browser only receives PNG images and JSON.

FEATURES

- Blink player with play/pause, step and speed control, each frame dated

- Zoom loupe with sharp, unblurred pixels

- Difference view: a moving source shows as a bright and dark pair

- Predicted track from catalogue proper motion, drawn on each frame's date

- Six detector arrays (0.75-5.0 microns) and false colour from three arrays

- Spectrum of the target across all arrays, with molecule band labels

- Bad-pixel flags overlay

- All-sky map: click anywhere to open that spot

- "Spot the mover" game, checked against the catalogue

- GIF export and shareable links; works on a phone; no login

- 20 built-in objects that play instantly, including Barnard's Star, WISE 0855, Epsilon Indi B, RW Aurigae, R Draconis, Proxima Centauri, the Orion Nebula and the Andromeda Galaxy

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

WiseView let volunteers find hundreds of moving objects in WISE data. SPHEREx re-observes the whole sky every six months in 102 colours, and no comparable public tool existed for it. SPHEREx Blink makes that data explorable by students, amateur astronomers and the curious, and shows what the mission's wavelength coverage adds: objects that only exist at certain colours.

WHAT IS CREATIVE

The motion we look for is 1-2 pixels, so the product is designed around making tiny changes visible. We also use SPHEREx's spectral dimension, not only time: array stepping, false colour and per-target spectra.

CURRENT STATE

The 20 built-in objects run entirely from the public site. Any other position is processed live from the archive by our open-source backend, which currently has to be run locally; a hosted backend is the next step.

TOOLS

Python, FastAPI, astropy, NumPy, Pillow; JavaScript, React; hosted on Vercel. Data from NASA SPHEREx via IRSA, proper motions from ESA Gaia DR3 and SIMBAD, name lookup by CDS Sesame. AI assistance (Claude) was used for coding, debugging, documentation and preparing the slides; all images are real SPHEREx data, not AI-generated.
